text:
rachel: Quick note from today's intro workshop: we hit a surprising auth behavior when students set REDWOOD_API_KEY + REDWOOD_PROJECT.

omar: what happened?

rachel: they put REDWOOD_API_KEY in their shell, then REDWOOD_PROJECT for the team. running the sample app showed env key logged then immediately replaced by a different key coming from project metadata.

pete: omg. so env var got silently overridden? that's definitely onboarding-unfriendly.

rachel: yep. logs: `Detected REDWOOD_API_KEY: pk_user_abc` then `Resolved project metadata -> using fallback pk_org_xyz`. Requests went to a different tenant.

omar: is this the resolver precedence bug? I thought env var should win unless user explicitly asked for project-managed credentials.

pete: agreed. expected order: CLI flag > env var > config file > project metadata/org default. sounds like ProjectProvider is short-circuiting.

rachel: exactly. short-term we told students to unset REDWOOD_PROJECT during the workshop. long-term we should change resolver to prefer explicit creds and only query project metadata when none are provided.

debug-bot: created DEVEX-3007: preserve env/flag creds over project metadata. linked to PR template.

omar: also proposing `rw auth:whoami` that prints source (flag|env|file|project-metadata) and `--explain` to show why a given key was chosen. would cut support noise.

pete: plus emit a telemetry event when project metadata would have overridden an explicit key so we can measure the impact.

docs: i'll add a short onboarding note in the sampleapp README advising not to set REDWOOD_PROJECT when following tutorials, and a troubleshooting entry: `rw auth:whoami` to confirm effective key.

rachel: perfect. can someone take the small fix? test matrix should include env+project, flag+project, and rotated project metadata cases.

omar: i'll own the PR. tiny change in auth/chain to check env/flag before calling ProjectProvider, add a console warning when there's a mismatch, tests, and `auth:whoami` CLI. will ping here when ready.

pete: thanks. this fixes a ton of confused workshop users. :tada:
